title: Affordable Capital-Stack Solver for Conversion Developers
one_liner: A structuring engine and expert memo that tells first-time affordable developers which subsidy stack is fundable for a given office conversion, with a calendar of deadlines.
customer: Office owners, small and mid developers and nonprofits pursuing conversions on public land or under affordability mandates, and city housing agencies running RFPs.
problem: Conversions are moving to public land and affordable set-asides (NYC's 100 Gold Street grew to 4,000 units with 1,000 affordable). That drags market-rate developers into a 6-8 source stack (4% LIHTC and bonds, land lease, abatements, historic credits, PACE, city and state gap funds) with volume-cap timing and set-aside tradeoffs. Consultants charge $25-75K and take months, and deals die before they start.
solution: Input a building and city, and get the top three feasible stacks with set-aside options, equity pricing ranges, application calendar and funder checklists. A human affordable-housing finance specialist reviews each output and delivers a structuring memo; an add-on kit supports public-land RFP responses.
why_now: The 2025 federal tax law eased the bond test for 4% credits and raised 9% allocations starting 2026. Conversions increasingly require affordability, and distressed-office buyers need a plan quickly.
revenue_model: $8-20K flat structuring memo, a 0.5% success fee on closed subsidy, and $1.5K per month developer subscription.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce input is not capital but a first-timer's knowledge of which stack is fundable and when. The winning product is an eligibility-and-calendar engine, not another architect's feasibility study.
first_30_days: Recruit two former affordable-housing finance directors. Publish stack templates for three cities with conversion incentives. Approach 20 office owners and receivers in those cities. Sell three memos at a $6K founder price.

title: Chosen-Kin Circles for Solo Agers
one_liner: Mutual health-care-proxy circles of 3-4 unrelated solo agers with legal packets and a professional backstop, sold as estate planning but delivering belonging.
customer: Adults 55-75 with no spouse or nearby children ($1,200 setup plus $29 a month), referred by elder-law and estate attorneys, and later employers' pre-retirement benefits and health systems.
problem: Trend chain: fewer children and more one-person households (29% of US households), then the first large kinless retirement cohort (roughly one in five older adults is an 'elder orphan' or at risk of becoming one), then hospitals default to statutory next of kin who may not exist or be estranged, ethics reviews and expensive guardianships follow, and nobody shows up. Loneliness and a legal vacuum arrive together.
solution: Match 3-4 members by neighborhood and temperament. Each signs reciprocal state-specific health-care proxy, HIPAA release, POA, pet-care and funeral-wishes documents. The circle meets quarterly at a facilitated dinner to refresh documents and check in. A professional fiduciary is the backstop, and a 24/7 dispatcher runs the call tree when a member is hospitalized, with a wallet card and QR link hospitals can scan.
why_now: The 2024-27 'Peak 65' wave brings about 4 million Americans a year into retirement, including the largest kinless cohort yet. LLM-assisted drafting made state-specific legal packets cheap. Loneliness is now a WHO-measured health metric, so systems are receptive.
revenue_model: Setup fee plus subscription, referral fees from attorneys, and enterprise deals where hospitals or plans pay to reduce unrepresented-patient cases.
non_obvious_insight: People will not pay for friends but will pay for a health-care proxy. Sell the legal and logistics wrapper and let belonging be the by-product. The documents make the circle real, because someone has promised to show up.
first_30_days: Partner with two estate-planning attorneys in one metro. Host three 'Circle Nights' at $299 per person including the document packet, and capture 30 members. Contract a fiduciary for the backstop.

title: Estate Planning for People's AI Agents
one_liner: Powers of attorney, dead-man switches and revocation tooling for the agents that hold standing authority over your money, email and subscriptions.
customer: Estate-planning attorneys and RIAs or family offices serving tech founders and executives who already run personal agents, followed by consumers through those channels.
problem: Personal agents now hold standing authority: card mandates, wallets, email access, autopay and negotiations. Step two: authority is tied to a living principal. Step three: death, incapacity, divorce or bankruptcy leaves agents acting on stale instructions or locks heirs out. Fiduciary access laws (for example RUFADAA) give no automatic access to digital accounts, and nobody has drafted for delegated software.
solution: An Agent Schedule for estate plans. It combines an inventory of agents, OAuth grants, wallets and mandates (via connectors), attorney-drafted clauses giving a digital fiduciary authority to pause, transfer or delete agents and limiting post-death actions, an incapacity or dead-man trigger that rotates credentials and downgrades permissions to read-only while notifying the fiduciary, and export of agent memory and logs for the executor.
why_now: Personal agents went mainstream in 2026 (OpenClaw reached about 247k GitHub stars), and agentic wallets and machine-payment rails launched in February and March 2026. The estate bar is only starting to publish AI afterlife primers, and they focus on AI personas, not delegated agents.
revenue_model: $500-$1,500 per client schedule sold through attorneys (roughly $300 wholesale), $10-$30/month monitoring, and $5k/year RIA channel licenses.
non_obvious_insight: Every technology that received delegated authority (checks, credit cards, cloud accounts) eventually got a legal instrument for the case where the principal stops existing. Agents have none yet, and the trigger events are guaranteed, so demand arrives on a calendar.
first_30_days: Draft the template with 2 estate attorneys. Pilot with 10 founders through an existing network. Build a simple inventory and revocation checklist using OAuth grant discovery for Google, Microsoft 365, GitHub and 5 agent platforms, and charge $750 per pilot.

title: Training-Day School Inside Youth Sports Facilities
one_liner: Turn the empty weekday hours of club-sports facilities into ESA- and scholarship-funded microschools for serious young athletes.
customer: Owners of independent indoor youth-sports facilities (volleyball, gymnastics, basketball, hockey, tennis/pickleball, swim) in ESA and voucher states such as AZ, FL, TX and UT. Tuition is paid by families out of ESA, voucher or (from 2027) scholarship-granting-organization funds.
problem: Facilities carry rent and HVAC costs but sit idle roughly 8am-3pm on weekdays, because their revenue is concentrated in evenings and weekends. Families spending thousands a year on club sports fight school schedules, travel and early mornings. Microschool compliance (registration, occupancy, insurance, ESA vendor status) is daunting for a gym owner. School status also matters financially: in Texas, registered private-school kids get about $10,474 in ESA money while homeschoolers get about $2,000.
solution: A turnkey 'training-day school' kit. It includes state-specific school registration and a change-of-occupancy checklist, a low-screen paper-based mastery curriculum from a partner, hiring and training of a credentialed lead teacher plus coach-guides, insurance, ESA/SGO vendor enrollment and tuition billing. The daily schedule is 3 hours of academics plus 3 hours of training. Opt-in wearable sleep and load data decides when the hard academic blocks and the hard training blocks fall. The facility fills 20-40 seats at ESA-level tuition during dead hours.
why_now: ESA money is scaling (Texas had 200k+ applicants). The federal $1,700 scholarship tax credit starts in 2027 with 31 states opted in, yet about 1,000 microschools are in limbo awaiting Treasury rules, so operators want ready-made compliance. Alpha School (about 50 campuses, heart-rate monitors) has shown parents will pay for short academics plus afternoon workshops. 61% of teachers now want less device use, and homeschooling is transient (about 30% do it for 1-2 years), so hybrid products fit.
revenue_model: $12-20k setup fee per facility plus 8-10% of tuition, or $1.5k/month SaaS plus billing fees. A site with 25 students at $8-10k is about $200-250k of tuition a year, so roughly $20k a year recurring to us per site. Add referral fees on curriculum and insurance.
non_obvious_insight: Alpha School sells a schedule, not a building. The scarcest inputs (a big safe space, coaches, motivated kids, parents with athletic budgets) already exist in every metro at sports facilities that lose money on weekdays. Boarding sports academies cost $70k+; the mid-market, ESA-priced version does not exist yet, and the gating constraint is building code, so the wedge is a compliance kit for the friendliest states.
first_30_days: Pick one state with microschool-friendly occupancy rules (for example Arizona or Florida). Contact 40 facility owners through club-owner groups and facility trade associations and sign 2-3 letters of intent. Pre-enroll 10-15 athlete families with $500 deposits for a January semester. Hire a part-time certified teacher as head of school, and use an existing curriculum partner plus a lawyer-reviewed compliance template.

title: Compliance-First CDL School Roll-Up for Carriers
one_liner: Buy the clean CDL schools that survived the federal crackdown, run them with AI scheduling and audit-ready records, and get paid per hired graduate by carriers.
customer: Trucking carriers (pay-per-hire or tuition guarantees), students (financed), and workforce boards. School owners are the sellers.
problem: FMCSA removed nearly 3,000 providers from the Training Provider Registry and has thousands more under investigation. The non-domiciled CDL rule effective 16 March 2026 removed an estimated 90,000+ CDLs. Carriers need legitimate, US-domiciled drivers with provable training, and independent schools are mom-and-pop operations with thin documentation, idle trucks and scarce instructors.
solution: Acquire mid-size schools with clean records. AI ops: scheduling that keeps trucks and instructors busy, automatic ELDT and registry records with an audit-ready evidence packet per student, simulators and camera or telematics coaching that shorten range hours, and a placement engine matching graduates to carriers. Carriers pay a bounty per hire and back student financing.
why_now: The 2026 crackdown turned record quality into a scarce, acquirable asset, and capacity is tight. Carriers want vetted sources of drivers, and simulators and telematics are now cheap.
revenue_model: Tuition of $4k to $8k per student (self-pay, financed, or WIOA-funded), carrier placement fees of $3k to $6k per hire, and simulator licensing to smaller schools.
non_obvious_insight: After a regulatory purge, provenance is the product. The school that can prove every training hour becomes a carrier's preferred feeder farm, so audit-ready data is worth more than the trucks. Reputation risk from CDL mills is a barrier to entry for bad actors and a marketing asset for a clean operator.
first_30_days: Sign a letter of intent with one small school owner on seller financing. Sign two regional carriers to a pilot pay-per-hired-graduate agreement. Put cameras and telematics on two training trucks and produce a sample audit packet. Publish pass and placement data.

title: Cross-Lab Calibration Plates for AI Training Data
one_liner: Ready-to-run reference plates and normalization software that make data from different labs, robots and cloud labs comparable enough to train models on.
customer: AI drug-discovery companies that merge internal, CRO and cloud-lab data, high-content screening groups, and cloud labs and CROs that want certified comparability.
problem: Trend chain: autonomous labs, cloud labs and philanthropic data programs multiply data streams. Models then cannot separate batch from biology. The JUMP Cell Painting consortium needed a 302-compound positive-control plate on every batch across 13 sites, and a cross-site organoid study found 2,188 differentially expressed genes by day 84. Physical reference standards for functional assays are not commercially supplied.
solution: Ship 'Reference Plate v1': lot-certified frozen reference cells (a defined iPSC-derived line at a fixed passage), the open JUMP-Target compound set, spike-ins and controls, all pre-plated. Customers run it on every batch. SaaS returns per-plate correction vectors, drift alarms and a 'harmonized to Reference v1' certificate. Expand to viability, high-content imaging and scRNA-seq perturbation assays.
why_now: Lila, Medra, Transfyr and other autonomous-lab efforts are producing data at scale. The OpenAI Foundation's $1B Public Data for Health grants will fund data generation whose cross-site comparability nobody audits. Batch-correction methods are mature, but no shared physical standard exists.
revenue_model: $250-600 per plate, $2-6k/month software, and $10-30k certification audits for labs and CROs.
non_obvious_insight: ERCC spike-ins and NIST-style standards made genomics data poolable. Functional assays lack an equivalent. Standards are winner-take-most: the first plate adopted by three or four major datasets becomes the de facto unit. Physical lots are also a moat that software-only AI shops cannot copy.
first_30_days: Source the JUMP-Target compound set. Produce 200 pilot plates. Give them free to 5 AI startups and cloud labs for a cross-site comparison. Publish the batch-variance reduction and convert the users to paid.

title: Shared-Aide Pods for 55+ Apartment Buildings
one_liner: One on-site aide team serves 6-10 residents in the same building, delivering assisted-living-style help at a fraction of 1:1 home-care cost.
customer: Owners and operators of independent-living and 55+ apartment buildings (market-rate, senior LIHTC and HUD-202 properties). The payers are middle-income residents and their families, who can't afford $75-130k a year and are stuck on waitlists.
problem: Home care is sold as one aide per client per hour ($35 an hour, about $80k a year for 44 hours a week) only because of legacy billing. Assisted living is at 90% occupancy with almost no new supply before 2030. Residents who age past independent living either move out or go without.
solution: A licensed home-care agency subsidiary (or partnership with one) posts 2-3 aides per shift inside the building. They run scheduled 15-45 minute ADL, medication-reminder, meal-setup and toileting visits, plus overnight response. Dispatch software handles acuity tiers and in-building routing (floors, elevators). Residents buy monthly tiers of about $1,800-3,500, and the property gets a retention amenity.
why_now: NIC MAP shows 57 of 99 metros above 90% occupancy, units under construction at a 2012 low, and no meaningful new supply before 2030. Medicaid HCBS is walled off by 15-month waitlists and labor is scarcer after the 2026 visa pause, so stretching each aide across more clients is the only lever left.
revenue_model: Monthly resident subscription by care tier, with a revenue share or amenity fee to the property owner. Later, Medicaid HCBS or managed-care billing for pods in affordable senior buildings.
non_obvious_insight: Aide hours are cheap to make dense (no drive time, no client-hour minimums) but are priced as if they were mobile. The gap between 1:1 pricing and 1:8 cost is the whole business, and only a property-anchored operator can capture it. Assisted-living-without-the-license is a real category nobody has scaled.
first_30_days: Sign a 90-day pilot with one 100-200 unit 55+ property in a tight market. Subcontract to an existing licensed agency to move quickly, staff a two-aide pod, and target 15 residents at about $2,200 a month. Track aide minutes per resident and move-out avoidance.

title: DKIM for Bank Accounts: Signed Payee Records
one_liner: A free, domain-verified payment record that suppliers publish, plus an AP plug-in that blocks any bank-detail change the supplier's own domain has not signed.
customer: Bookkeeping and accounting firms, and AP teams at 20-500 person companies on QuickBooks, Xero, Bill.com or NetSuite. Suppliers publish for free.
problem: BEC cost $3.05B in 2025, about 3.4x the $893M IC3 tags as AI-related, yet the money and attention go to deepfake detection. Bank-detail change requests still arrive by email or phone and get 'verified' by calling a number supplied in the same message. Small firms have no fraud team, and 3 seconds of audio now clones the voice they trust.
solution: A supplier proves domain control (DNS TXT plus a signed JSON file: legal name, hashed account and routing numbers, valid-from and valid-to dates, rotation contacts). A browser extension and accounting-app add-on compares any vendor bank details at bill entry and payment approval against that record. It hard-warns on mismatch and routes changes through a supplier-initiated, delayed, out-of-band confirmation flow. Every check is logged as evidence for the firm's crime-insurance social-engineering endorsement.
why_now: Cloned voices and AI-written invoices have broken the callback-and-voice-check control. IC3's 2025 numbers show BEC is still the largest business loss pool. Instant rails like FedNow and RTP make wrong payments irrevocable. Accounting platforms now have open app stores that allow a third-party control at the moment of payment.
revenue_model: $5-9 per client company per month for accounting firms, or $19-29 per AP seat for in-house teams. Suppliers are free. Later, per-check API fees from payment platforms and insurer-funded discounts.
non_obvious_insight: BEC is a provenance problem for one string of digits, not a media-authenticity problem. Email fraud fell when SPF/DKIM anchored trust in domain ownership, and the same move works for payee data. Selling through accountants avoids the two-sided cold start: each supplier who publishes instantly protects every customer of theirs that uses a participating firm.
first_30_days: Publish an open spec, a Chrome extension and a read-only Xero/QuickBooks add-on. Recruit 10-15 bookkeeping firms (30-100 clients each) through ProAdvisor and bookkeeper communities. For each firm, send its 20 largest vendors a five-minute publish flow. Convert 10 firms to $99/month plans.

title: SpaceX Exposure Verification Desk for Advisors
one_liner: A due-diligence service that tells advisors and retail investors whether a 'SpaceX exposure' SPV actually holds anything, and flags impersonation and deepfake endorsements timed to launch and IPO news.
customer: Registered investment advisers, family offices, broker-dealer compliance teams and private-bank due-diligence desks being pitched SPVs and notes marketed as SpaceX or Starlink exposure. Secondary: sophisticated retail via a subscription.
problem: Demand for SpaceX exposure is intense (Starlink about 12M subscribers, $11.4B 2025 revenue, Starship reached orbit on 28 Sept 2026), but shares are transfer-restricted, so anything offered is indirect: SPVs of SPVs with stacked fees, sold over LinkedIn, WhatsApp and Telegram, some holding nothing. Deepfake Musk endorsements and fake launch livestreams add a scam layer. Lumpy events such as the 16 Sept 2026 Valor distribution add confusion about what is real.
solution: (1) Map every SPV using SpaceX or Starlink naming from SEC Form D and adviser filings, with sponsor history, fee stacks and upstream fund lineage. (2) Holdings attestation by obtaining custodian, transfer agent or upstream-fund confirmation. (3) Compare marketing claims against issuer transfer restrictions and last known tender pricing. (4) A red-flag score (offshore layers, unlicensed sellers, cloned domains) and an alert feed on new offerings and impersonation around launch days and any listing.
why_now: IPO speculation, the Valor stock distribution on 16 Sept 2026, Starship's orbital flight and a record Golden Dome and launch boom are all feeding retail FOMO. Scam economics are inverting (tools cost about $50 while average payments rose 253%) and AI deepfakes are cheap. If a listing happens, the desk pivots to lock-up and SPV-unwind verification, so it does not depend on one date.
revenue_model: $750-2,500 per SPV verification report, $499 per month for adviser subscriptions with alerts, and enterprise seats for compliance teams. Later expansion to other hot pre-IPO space names.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce thing is not access to SpaceX but the truth about what an SPV holds. The key facts (Form D filings, fee layers, issuer restrictions) are public and cheap to analyze, yet every hype cycle mints exposure products faster than compliance staff can diligence. Buyers pay for a signed opinion that gives them cover to say no.
first_30_days: Scrape EDGAR for SpaceX and Starlink SPV names and publish an 'SPV Layer Map' with fee stacks. Send it to 200 RIAs and compliance officers. Offer 3 free verifications, then sell the next ones at $1,500. Set up domain-impersonation monitoring keyed to launch dates. Position as research and diligence, not investment advice.

title: Rent-a-Robot Creature Actors for Haunts and Events
one_liner: A rental troupe of costumed quadruped and humanoid robots, with operators and safety systems, for haunted attractions, festivals, conventions and immersive shows.
customer: Haunted attractions, seasonal theme-park events, festivals and conventions, immersive theatre producers and brand activations.
problem: Haunts struggle to hire and retain actors, and scares repeat. Fans love character robots (Disney's droids), but building one is expensive and risky, so small producers cannot offer them.
solution: Buy off-the-shelf sub-$5k quadrupeds and $6-16k humanoids and fit them with fabricated creature shells. Add a director's tablet for scripted and remote-driven behaviors, geofencing and e-stops, and insurance. Rent at $800-2,500 per night with an operator.
why_now: Cheap quadrupeds and humanoids with open-source locomotion are available, entertainment robots are already common in China, and Halloween is five weeks away.
revenue_model: Nightly rental plus operator fee, then creature shell and kit sales and character licensing.
non_obvious_insight: The hard part is not the robot, it is the show: safety envelope, character design, logistics and insurance. Amortizing hardware over 100+ nights a year makes this a creature-troupe service business, not a robotics company.
first_30_days: Lease 2 robots for about $6k and build two creature shells. Book 3-5 haunts and one convention for October and November at about $1,000 per night. Get event insurance and a written safety protocol.

title: Distressed Cargo Rescue Desk for Bankrupt Importers
one_liner: A broker-run desk that takes orphaned containers from failed importers, clears the four-way legal tangle in days, and delivers the goods to off-price buyers at deep discounts.
customer: Off-price retailers, closeout buyers and liquidators who cannot currently buy orphaned cargo because they are not the consignee. Carriers and CFS operators, who want the boxes gone, and trustees, who want recovery, are the supply side. The buyer pays a handling fee or a spread.
problem: When a small importer fails mid-shipment, the goods sit on the water or on a terminal with no ISF, no entry, no bond and a demurrage and storage clock running. The bills of lading are in a dead company's name. Carriers and warehouses will not release cargo to strangers. Buyers would pay well for the goods but cannot make entry. Unentered cargo can be sent to a General Order warehouse after about 15 days and is subject to public sale after roughly six months, so value bleeds out. Many boxes are eventually abandoned, auctioned for pennies or destroyed. The 2025-26 tariff whiplash left a long tail of failed importers, and Long Beach's record volumes keep yard space and free time expensive.
solution: Run a cargo rescue desk with five steps. (1) Source: call carriers' demurrage collection desks, CFS warehouses in Carson and Long Beach, and bankruptcy trustees to find orphaned cargo. (2) Screen: triage compliance risk (CPSC certification, FDA, FCC, UFLPA and IPR issues) and refuse any box that cannot be legally sold. (3) Title: obtain the trustee's or owner's transfer of cargo rights and a negotiated carrier release, trading the removal of the box for a waiver or reduction of demurrage. (4) Entry: the purchaser, as an actual purchaser with the right to make entry, becomes importer of record on a single-transaction bond, with a licensed broker filing the entry. (5) Deliver to the buyer's warehouse. Where the invoices are non-compliant, a dispute of the demurrage under the FMC's billing rules adds leverage.
why_now: Small-brand failures peaked through the 2025 tariff shock and its aftershocks. The IEEPA reversal of Feb 2026 has estates now holding refund cash but still holding stranded physical goods. Off-price retail demand for cheap inventory is high. Single-transaction customs bonds mean a new team does not need a continuous bond or big capital to start.
revenue_model: 10-15% handling and sourcing fee on landed cost from the buyer, or a resale spread on consignment goods. Add trustee-side success fees where the desk increases estate recovery. Duties and fees are pre-funded by the buyer, so the desk avoids inventory risk in the early phase.
non_obvious_insight: A container of orphaned goods is worth its inventory value minus the clock. The party that can solve four separate systems (bill-of-lading rights, the carrier lien and demurrage, customs entry and IOR, and compliance screening) in days captures the discount. VCs treat liquidation as a marketplace problem. It is a legal-plumbing problem, and only a customs broker knows how the entry, bond and purchaser-as-IOR pieces fit together.
first_30_days: Line up a partner bond agent for single-transaction bonds and one buyer network of 5-10 off-price and closeout buyers. Call demurrage collections and terminal-side contacts at 10 carriers and 10 CFS warehouses with a simple offer: we clear abandoned cargo if you waive charges. Ask two bankruptcy trustees whether any estate holds cargo. Close the first 2-3 rescues in the 30-60 day window with fully buyer-funded duties.

title: Opt-Out Time Machine for AI Training Compliance
one_liner: A historical archive of every site's machine-readable AI-training opt-outs (robots.txt, TDMRep, ai.txt, meta tags, headers) so model builders can prove what was reserved on the day they crawled.
customer: AI startups and labs that train or fine-tune on scraped or third-party data (especially EU-exposed), dataset publishers, and rights-holder groups (publishers, collecting societies) that need proof of their own reservations.
problem: GPAI obligations have applied since Aug 2025 and AI Office enforcement began in Aug 2026. Providers need a copyright policy and must respect machine-readable rights reservations under the EU text-and-data-mining exception (background, verify). Opt-out signals change over time and nobody retains neutral evidence of what a site said on a given day, yet disputes will turn on exactly that.
solution: A weekly crawl of the top ~50M domains capturing robots.txt, /.well-known/tdmrep.json, ai.txt, meta tags, headers and terms-page hashes, stored as signed, timestamped snapshots. API calls answer 'what did domain X reserve at time T?' and 'filter dataset D by reservations as of T'. Certificates of compliance for training corpora and monitoring alerts for rights holders whose reservations are ignored.
why_now: Enforcement powers over GPAI providers began Aug 2026, copyright-and-training cases are moving through European courts, and crawl and storage costs are low enough for a two-person team.
revenue_model: API subscriptions of $2-25k/month for labs and dataset teams, $5-30k per compliance certificate, and $500-5k/month for rights-holder monitoring.
non_obvious_insight: Compliance evidence is a time-series problem. The neutral party that started archiving earlier owns the truth, and it cannot be recreated retroactively, so the moat begins accumulating on day one.
first_30_days: Crawl the top 1M domains weekly (a few hundred dollars a month) and publish a free opt-out prevalence report. Sign three EU AI startups or dataset publishers to paid pilots of $2-5k and approach one collecting society.

title: Pay Home Inspectors to Find Lead Pipes
one_liner: A micro-bounty network that pays home inspectors, plumbers and water-heater installers to photograph where the service line enters the basement, with AI classification, so utilities can clear 'unknown material' lines for about $40 each instead of $500-3,000 each.
customer: Mid-size municipal and district water utilities (20k-300k connections) with a large 'unknown material' share in their published lead service line inventory. The buyer is the utility director or the lead program manager. A secondary payer is the home buyer, who pays about $29 for a 'Lead Line Certificate' add-on at inspection.
problem: Since the lead and copper inventory requirement, every system has had to classify each service line as lead, galvanized-requiring-replacement, non-lead or unknown. Unknowns are a legal and financial liability, and they are hard to shrink. The only sure verification is potholing or excavation, which costs hundreds to thousands of dollars per line. Customer self-ID by mailer gets a response rate of roughly 10-25%. Absentee landlords and LLCs almost never answer. Utility crews can't look inside private basements, so tens of thousands of unknowns sit in the spreadsheet for years.
solution: A mobile app with a fixed 3-photo protocol: the pipe where it enters the building, a scratch or magnet test close-up, and the meter serial number with the address. A vision model classifies the pipe as copper, galvanized, lead, PEX, PVC or HDPE, or flags it as unresolved. Humans QA the low-confidence cases. Each submission is geo-verified and tamper-evident, and exports in the format the state inventory portal expects. Inspectors and plumbers earn $15-25 per verified line, and the platform earns the spread. The utility gets a reconciled inventory feed and a dashboard showing unknowns falling by ZIP code. The consumer add-on (inspector-branded certificate, sold to the buyer) pays the inspector while giving the utility free data.
why_now: The first inventories were filed in late 2024, and public analyses showed millions of lines still classified 'unknown'. The Lead and Copper Rule Improvements set a 10-year replacement clock that starts around 2027, though federal details keep being revisited and litigated. Several states have their own replacement statutes that don't depend on the federal rule. The $15B in dedicated infrastructure-law lead line money is moving through state revolving funds under spend-down pressure. Vision models are only now accurate enough to classify pipe photos. (Regulatory details are from memory. Verify state acceptance rules before pitching.)
revenue_model: Utilities pay $30-60 per verified line, sold as a per-line contract that fits under small-purchase thresholds. A $10-25k pilot is typical, followed by annual contracts. The consumer-paid certificate ($29) is split with the inspector. Later products are inventory-reconciliation SaaS and an access-agreement workflow for replacement crews.
non_obvious_insight: Utilities think they have a data problem, but they have an eyeballs-in-basements problem. Every home sale (an inspector visits) and every water heater swap (a plumber stands three feet from the service entry) already puts a paid expert next to the exact pipe that matters. Nobody has paid them for a photo yet. Excavation is the wrong tool for a question that visual inspection answers for almost nothing.
first_30_days: Pick one state that accepts documented visual or contractor verification. Pick two utilities in it whose public inventories are more than 40% unknown. Recruit 30 inspectors through local InterNACHI and ASHI chapter meetups and Facebook groups, and pay a launch bonus per photo set. Run a 200-line pilot. Have the utility pothole 30 of those lines as ground truth, then publish the accuracy numbers. Close a $15-25k pilot purchase order with the first utility, using the small-purchase limit that many cities set at $25-50k so no council vote is needed.

title: Scam Fire Drills: A Security Detail for Grandparents
one_liner: Wealthy families run kidnap and extortion protocols with duress words and a 24/7 first-response team; for $20/mo, give ordinary families rehearsed scam drills and a 15-minute fraud hotline, funded partly by the banks that eat the losses.
customer: Adult children (35-55) with parents 70+, and the credit unions and community banks that sponsor the service for older members. The buyer pays $20/mo per family, or a bank pays $3-6 per enrolled member.
problem: FTC data shows consumers reported $15.9B in fraud losses in 2025, with people 50+ reporting $4.3B and impersonation scams over $3.5B. Awareness campaigns fail because panic overrides knowledge in the moment, and identity-monitoring products act after the money is gone. Recovery windows (wire recalls, gift-card and crypto-ATM freezes, ACH returns) are hours long, and most victims do not know the first-hour steps.
solution: Family onboarding: credit freezes for all members, passkeys and a password manager, SIM-swap locks, a family safe word, and trusted-contact registration at banks. Quarterly consented drills: a scripted call using a synthetic voice (never a relative's cloned voice) tests how the parent responds to a 'grandchild in jail' or 'bank fraud department' scenario, with coaching afterward. A 24/7 hotline answers within 15 minutes with a step-by-step recovery playbook, initiating wire recall, card dispute and gift-card issuer calls while the money can still be clawed back.
why_now: AI voice cloning has made grandparent and executive-impersonation scams cheap, and 2025 losses jumped by a quarter or more from 2024. Credit unions are actively seeking member-protection programs; for example, Illinois law from 1 January 2026 lets credit union staff contact a member's listed trusted person when exploitation is suspected.
revenue_model: $20/mo per family; $3-6 per member per month from credit unions and community banks (reduced fraud losses and liability, and a retention benefit); referral fees on identity-theft insurance and data-broker removal partners.
non_obvious_insight: Rehearsal, not awareness, changes behavior under panic, exactly as fire drills do; nobody sells consented scam simulations to families. The first-hour response is where dollars are actually saved, so a human hotline is the product, and the party with the strongest incentive to pay is the financial institution that absorbs the loss.
first_30_days: Recruit 20 families through parent-of-aging-parents communities and run a manual onboarding call plus one drill each with a contract fraud analyst on call. Record the drill failure rate as a headline stat. Pitch two local credit unions on a 100-member sponsored pilot, priced at $4 per member per month.

title: By Heart: Memorization Recitals as Status
one_liner: A membership club where knowledge workers memorize whole works and perform them at ticketed, witnessed recital nights, making 'held in my head' the new marathon medal.
customer: Affluent 28-55 year old knowledge workers (lawyers, designers, engineers, execs) who feel their minds going soft from AI offloading. Secondary buyers are hosts who want a 'living book' at a dinner, and companies booking offsites.
problem: Retrieval and summarization are now free and instant, so 'I know X' signals nothing. Bodies have legible, socially rewarded proof of discipline (marathons, Whoop scores, Hyrox). Minds have none. The 'cognitive debt' discourse around AI use is producing anxiety, but there is no communal, visible way to do something about it.
solution: 8-week cohorts with a memory coach and a deliberately text-hiding spaced-repetition app (no AI recall aids). A 'Canon' of about 60 pieces: sonnets, a Rilke elegy, Book IV of the Aeneid in translation, the Gettysburg Address, a language's 500 proverbs. Progress levels (100 lines, 500, 1,000, a whole play). Each level ends in a public recital in a bar or library, with two strangers in the audience co-signing a 'Held' certificate. A leaderboard tracks lines held. High-tier patrons book private salons where a member recites at dinner.
why_now: By 2026 the MIT Media Lab 'Your Brain on ChatGPT' study and the 'cognitive debt' idea have become mainstream (Psychology Today, Substack, Medium), and poetry-memorization essays are circulating as a counter-movement. Chat agents now do everything except being you. Run clubs, pickleball, and social-fitness scenes show demand for communal costly-signal hobbies. Nobody has built the cognitive equivalent.
revenue_model: $45/month membership. $199 cohort fees. $25-40 recital tickets. $1,500-5,000 for private 'living book' salons. $8-15k corporate offsite packages. Later, certified coach licensing.
non_obvious_insight: Status flows to whatever is costly, public, and impossible to outsource. Memory just became that, the way running became status once cars made walking optional. The proof is a witnessed live performance, which AI cannot fake and which needs no equipment, so it is a democratic status game with a cheap entry fee.
first_30_days: Run three free recital nights at a bar or library in one city and recruit about 20 people. Pre-sell a 6-week $199 cohort. Recruit 2-3 theater or memory-sport coaches on rev-share. Run everything on Notion and an existing flashcard tool. Target 30 paid members and 2 private salon bookings by day 90.

title: Notary Network as the Proof-of-Human Layer for Hiring
one_liner: Use the millions of already-commissioned notaries as in-person witnesses who certify that a remote job candidate is a real, physically present person and not a deepfake or proxy.
customer: Security and talent-acquisition leads at remote-first companies (50-2,000 employees) hiring engineers, finance and IT-admin roles, plus crypto and fintech firms, staffing agencies and BPOs onboarding remote workers. Paid per candidate.
problem: Real-time face-swap tools, proxy interviewees and North Korean IT-worker schemes (with DOJ takedowns of US 'laptop farms' in 2025) defeat video interviews and selfie-liveness KYC. Gartner has predicted that one in four candidate profiles could be fake by 2028. Big companies have reportedly brought back in-person final rounds, but a 60-person remote startup has no office to bring anyone to.
solution: A dispatch flow on top of existing mobile-notary and signing-agent networks. The candidate meets a notary in person, at a UPS Store, coworking space or their home. The notary checks physical ID and signs a jurat-style attestation, and the candidate's device is paired to a session key. The notary sits with them for the proctored final technical interview, or witnesses laptop receipt and first login. The employer receives a signed, legally meaningful 'Verified Human Presence' certificate to attach to the ATS, HRIS and payroll. Priced at $79-149 per candidate, with the notary paid $40-70.
why_now: Deepfake fraud in hiring became a mainstream security topic in 2025-26. Enforcement actions against laptop farms have made boards care. Remote-notary and mobile-notary dispatch marketplaces already have the workflow tooling, and ATS platforms now expose APIs and partner directories. Digital-identity vendors are all software-only and share the same weakness against generative video.
revenue_model: Per-verification fee; an ATS-integration subscription (Greenhouse, Ashby, Lever); annual re-verification for employees with privileged access; enterprise bundles for staffing agencies and BPOs.
non_obvious_insight: Notaries are the only large, already-bonded, already-commissioned network of humans whose legal job is to certify that a person was physically in front of them. Identity vendors overlooked them because they assumed software would replace presence. When faces become forgeable, presence attestation becomes the premium product, and the distribution network already exists and needs no capital to build.
first_30_days: Build a simple booking and attestation web flow. Sign up two mobile-notary networks or about 40 individual notaries across SF, NYC, Austin, Seattle and Chicago. Recruit 15-20 security-conscious remote-first startups through CISO and hiring-fraud communities. Charge $99 and complete 50 verifications. Publish anonymized 'fraud caught' case studies to drive inbound.

title: Green-Claims Clearance for EU-Bound Brands
one_liner: A crawl-and-fix service that strips or substantiates banned 'eco-friendly' and 'climate-neutral' claims on packaging, product pages and ads for brands selling into the EU.
customer: DTC brands, Amazon and Shopify sellers, and mid-size consumer-goods companies selling to EU consumers, plus their marketing agencies and EU authorised representatives.
problem: Directive (EU) 2024/825 applies from 27 Sept 2026. It bans generic environmental claims ('green', 'eco-friendly') without recognised excellent performance, bans offset-based 'climate neutral' claims, and restricts sustainability labels to certified or public schemes. Small brands have thousands of SKUs of copy across 24 languages and no clear way to check it.
solution: Crawl product pages, packaging PDFs and ad libraries, flag banned and risky patterns in 24 languages, and suggest compliant rewrites with evidence-pack templates (life-cycle summary, certification proof). Add a human legal-review tier and monitoring of competitors' claims for complaint filing.
why_now: The rule began applying on 27 Sept 2026, and member-state transposition laws are now in force. The separate Green Claims Directive was shelved, so consultancies shifted attention, yet this ban is already law and cheap to police by machine.
revenue_model: $1-5k initial audit, $300-1,500 per month monitoring, and agency white-label licences.
non_obvious_insight: This is a deadline-driven, per-SKU checking problem that suits software plus a thin human legal layer, and the first enforcement will often start with competitor complaints. The best lead-gen is showing a brand its own violations.
first_30_days: Build a claims lexicon in five languages. Scan the top 200 product categories on Amazon.de and .fr for violations. Email brand founders their own violations as a free preview. Partner with three EU marketing agencies.

title: Human Baseline Vault for AI Detection
one_liner: Proctored, ID-verified, unassisted human writing and speech, timestamped and sealed, sold first as ground truth for detector calibration and later as low-background evaluation data.
customer: AI-detection vendors, ed-tech firms and publishers, university integrity offices, trust-and-safety teams, and AI labs' evaluation teams.
problem: Studies report detector false-positive rates of 5-20% on native English and up to 61% on non-native writing. 25+ universities have restricted detectors, and a February 2026 New York court ordered Adelphi to expunge a student's AI accusation. Vendors cannot prove error rates by population because clean post-2022 human ground truth is unknowable, since everyone's 'human' data may be AI-assisted.
solution: Recruit 20k+ verified people across strata (non-native English, neurodivergent, technical, legal and academic writers, age bands) to write and speak in proctored sessions. Samples are timestamped and hash-anchored. Sell calibration sets and per-population false-positive certificates to detector vendors, then an annually refreshed vault as 'low-background steel' for evaluations and future disputes.
why_now: Over half of web traffic is automated and training and evaluation sets are increasingly contaminated. Lawsuits and university bans mean detector buyers now need error rates by population, and AI labs need uncontaminated human evaluation data.
revenue_model: $50-250k dataset licences, $20-75k per detector audit and certificate, and annual refresh subscriptions.
non_obvious_insight: Like pre-1945 steel free of nuclear fallout, verified pre-contamination human data gets more valuable every year, and its value lies in the chain of custody, not the text itself.
first_30_days: Recruit 500 participants through two university partners for a native versus non-native pilot. Pitch two detector vendors and one ed-tech firm. Publish an independent study on false positives by population to earn press.

title: Robot Bullies: Paid Adversarial Pedestrian Panels
one_liner: A vetted panel of paid 'difficult humans' who kick, block, crowd and confuse sidewalk robots and humanoids on a controlled test range, so robot makers find their failures before the public does.
customer: Sidewalk delivery robot operators, humanoid and AMR makers preparing EU conformity files and retail or warehouse pilots, city permit offices that want interaction evidence, and robot insurers. First buyers are the safety or field-ops leads at 20 to 50 mid-size robot companies.
problem: Robots fail on human behavior, not physics. In 2026 an Uber Eats delivery robot was kicked over in Philadelphia, and robots circled in confusion in Lincoln Park in September. Each robot costs about $2,500 to replace, and the backlash is turning into permit fights. Makers test with polite employees or dummies. Nobody sells honest, repeatable samples of teens, drunks, kids, dog-walkers and wheelchair users behaving badly around a machine.
solution: A rented lot or closed street block set up as a 'behavior range', with a library of scripted provocations (path blocking, tailgating, encirclement by six teens, camera covering, gentle-force shoves, darting child-sized mannequins, cane and wheelchair users, leashed dogs). Screened, consented, insured participants are paid per session. Cameras and force sensors record everything. The output is a report formatted for conformity files and city permit filings, plus a recurring regression-testing subscription. Later: an anonymized 'Chaos Index' that ranks robot models by how they hold up against human misbehavior.
why_now: Sidewalk robots are now numerous enough to cause visible backlash, with the Philadelphia kicking incidents and the Lincoln Park swarm video. The EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 applies from 20 January 2027. ISO 25785-1, the first safety standard for legged and actively balanced robots, is still a draft, so makers have nothing to test against. Humanoid pilots are starting in warehouses and stores.
revenue_model: Test days at $8k to $25k per protocol set. Annual regression-testing subscriptions from $120k. Rev share with certification bodies (TUV, UL) on referred test packages. Licensing of anonymized behavior data to simulation and model teams.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce input is not test-track capacity. It is honest human misbehavior at scale, and no simulator or employee panel produces it. The moat is the clinical-trial-style infrastructure: consent forms, insurance, screening and a bench of reliable trouble-makers. Robot makers will pay more for a 16-year-old's creativity than for another simulator.
first_30_days: Rent a parking lot on weekends. Recruit 30 paid participants from campus job boards at about $30 per hour. Have a lawyer draft consent forms and buy $2M of general liability. Pitch one local sidewalk-robot operator or university warehouse-robot startup a $5k to $10k 'chaos day' with a written report. Publish a free 'Chaos Report' on the Philadelphia-style behaviors to generate inbound leads.

title: Fire-Loss Data Co-op and Parametric MRF Cover
one_liner: Pool waste-facility fire data to price the unpriced battery-fire risk, then offer verified premium credits and fast-paying parametric cover.
customer: MRFs, transfer stations, scrap yards and e-scrap recyclers (pay verification and premium), with specialty brokers, MGAs and reinsurers buying the data.
problem: August 2026 saw 49 facility fires (tied for the 10-year August high), 293 year to date, and 74 catastrophic (over $400K) versus 71 in all of 2024. Public counts cover only two-alarm-plus events, and actual totals may be about 6x higher. Severe incidents average about $1.5M and no one has decided who pays.
solution: Step 1 is a fire-risk score and controls-verification certificate (thermal cameras, suppression, inbound inspection, tip-floor separation). Step 2 is an anonymized incident and thermal-alert data co-op. Step 3 is an MGA arrangement with a fronting carrier offering premium credits for verified controls and a parametric top-up that pays a fixed amount when a verified thermal event crosses a threshold, for fast cleanup and business-interruption cash.
why_now: Losses are concentrating and rising, states are still arguing about liability, and BRACE Act storage-permit debates put battery handling in the spotlight. The expected next step is insurers repricing, adding exclusions or demanding sensors, so verified data becomes the currency.
revenue_model: $2-5K per site per year for verification, a 10-15% MGA commission on placed premium, and data licensing to insurers and reinsurers.
non_obvious_insight: The unpriced risk here is data, not fire physics. The industry's own public numbers understate reality by roughly 6x, so the first party with a real loss dataset sets the price.
first_30_days: Compile a scrubbed fire dataset from trackers, news, fire-department reports and OSHA logs and derive loss-cost bands. Interview 5 specialty brokers. Recruit 5 facilities for a pilot with an off-the-shelf thermal camera package. Open talks with a fronting carrier.

title: Court-Ready Deepfake Authenticity Reports for Lawyers
one_liner: $500-1,500, 48-hour forensic reports on disputed audio, video, screenshots and voicemails, written to survive an authenticity challenge.
customer: Solo and small family-law, employment and criminal-defence firms, insurer special-investigation units, and HR investigators.
problem: Cloned-voice voicemails and fabricated chats now appear in custody and harassment disputes. The proposed federal evidence rules on deepfakes (901(c)) and machine-generated evidence (707) have stalled, and in June 2026 the Standing Committee sent 707 back for further study, so judges decide case by case. Bespoke forensic experts cost $5-20k and take weeks.
solution: A productised workflow: intake with chain of custody, multiple detectors plus provenance checks (metadata, C2PA, compression history, device and source-app fingerprints), review and a signed declaration from a credentialed examiner, optional testimony, and template motions on authentication for lawyers.
why_now: Cheap voice cloning has moved from fraud into family and employment disputes. The federal rule process has stalled, leaving a gap that judges and lawyers must fill with experts, and lawyers face sanctions if they present unverified AI evidence.
revenue_model: $500-1,500 per report, $2-5k per day for testimony, and a $299 per month firm plan that includes three reports.
non_obvious_insight: Detection accuracy is weak everywhere. The scarce thing is a credentialed human willing to sign under oath with a documented method. Productise the signature and the paper trail, and treat detectors as inputs.
first_30_days: Recruit three forensic audio and video examiners. Sell through local family-law bar associations and CLE talks. Publish three anonymised case studies and a report template reviewed by trial attorneys.

title: Certified Raw Milk: Testing, Herdshares, Insurance
one_liner: The neutral assurance layer for the gray-legal raw milk market: weekly pathogen and H5N1 testing, herdshare paperwork, and the first insurable 'tested farm' program.
customer: Small dairies (roughly 5-100 cows) that sell raw milk through herdshares or state-permitted on-farm sales. Later, surplus-lines insurers and MGAs, and consumers who scan a batch QR code.
problem: Demand for raw milk is rising with the wellness and MAHA-era food politics, but farms run with no shared safety standard, no liability coverage, and thin legal paperwork. Herdshares are a legal workaround that state attorneys general and FDA (on interstate sales) increasingly scrutinize as disguised retail. H5N1 in dairy herds since 2024 and USDA's national milk-testing strategy raised the stakes. One sick customer can end a farm.
solution: A subscription with four parts. (1) Scheduled bulk-tank sampling, with a partner state-accredited lab running a pathogen panel (Salmonella, Listeria, STEC, Campylobacter) plus H5N1 PCR. (2) A public farm page and batch QR code that show results, including failures. (3) State-specific herdshare agreements and an incident-response protocol, reviewed by counsel. (4) After 6-12 months of data, a group liability policy priced off each farm's test history.
why_now: H5N1 in US dairy cattle (2024-26) made pathogen testing a mainstream topic. Federal and state milk-testing programs are expanding. Raw milk politics are at a high, and 2026 reporting shows FDA pressure on interstate sales and closer AG review of herdshare contracts. Farms now need a defensible paper trail, and insurers have no data to price this risk.
revenue_model: $150-400 per farm per month for testing and certification, with lab costs around 40%. Per-batch certificate fees. A 10-15% commission or MGA fee on group liability premiums once claims data exists. Optional $5/month 'verified member' fee paid by herdshare customers.
non_obvious_insight: Raw milk's growth is capped by trust and insurability, not demand. Insurers, retailers and regulators won't touch it because nobody can prove anything. The winner is not a milk brand but the certifier (think UL or organic certification) that publishes failures. Believers and skeptics can both trust that, and the test history becomes the underwriting dataset that unlocks insurance, which is the real moat.
first_30_days: Pick one state with a strong raw-milk farmer network and clear legal footing (for example Pennsylvania or Utah). Recruit 10-15 farms through state raw-milk associations and Farm-to-Consumer Legal Defense Fund events. Sign a wholesale rate with an accredited lab. Sell a $199/month 'weekly test plus public results page' pilot. Show 3 months of data to 2 surplus-lines brokers to scope a group liability program.

title: Arc-Flash and Protection Studies Factory
one_liner: Deliver PE-stamped short-circuit, coordination and arc-flash studies in days rather than months, using AI to turn photos and one-lines into models.
customer: Electrical contractors and EPCs building C&I storage, EV depots and data center electrical rooms, plus facility managers facing five-year label refreshes.
problem: Power-systems engineers are scarce and studies gate energization and permits, with 8-12 week backlogs. A delayed 60 MW site costs about $3M a week. NFPA 70E requires reassessment every five years, and small C&I storage projects cannot afford $30k custom studies.
solution: Studies as a productized service. The contractor uploads single-line diagrams, nameplate photos and the utility fault-current letter. AI extracts the equipment and builds the ETAP or SKM model, a licensed PE reviews and stamps it, and the customer gets labels and coordination settings on a five-business-day SLA at a flat price per switchboard.
why_now: Vision and language models now parse one-lines and nameplates well enough to draft models. The data center and storage boom, and the engineer shortage, make throughput the scarce resource.
revenue_model: $3-15k per small C&I study, $30-100k per data center study, and recurring five-year renewals plus label printing.
non_obvious_insight: Nobody lacks software. They lack stamps and turnaround time. PE-supervised throughput with AI drafts is a labor arbitrage that stays unglamorous enough to avoid heavy competition.
first_30_days: Recruit two retired power-systems PEs. Build the extraction pipeline on 20 anonymized one-lines. Sell five C&I storage installers a $4k fixed-price study with a five-day SLA. Measure margins.

title: Lot-Level Reagent Reliability Oracle for Buyer Agents
one_liner: A neutral, pooled 'Carfax for reagent lots' that tells human and agent buyers whether this specific lot of serum, Matrigel, antibody or PBMC has worked in other labs before they order it.
customer: Cell-culture, organoid and iPSC labs at startups, CROs and universities. API customers are lab-procurement and ELN agents that place orders. Buyers are lab managers and platform teams with a per-lab subscription.
problem: Lot-to-lot variability is the tribal knowledge of biology. Matrigel has about 1,800 proteins and is specified only as 8-22 mg/mL, and a cross-site study found 2,188 differentially expressed genes by day 84. Labs test-and-reserve serum lots and trade warnings on Slack. Certificates of analysis do not predict downstream performance. Autonomous purchasing and ELN agents will happily reorder the cheapest 'equivalent' lot with no lore, and agents repeating analyses already vary stochastically. Pharma cannot pool this data across competitors.
solution: An opt-in ELN/LIMS plug-in and Slack bot logs only lot number, cell line or assay type and a coarse outcome flag (grew, differentiated, failed QC). It pools this anonymized across subscribers into a lot-performance ledger. Humans and agents query it by MCP or API before ordering ('lot X failed iPSC-organoid differentiation in 4 of 9 labs') and get alerts if a lot already in their freezer turns bad. The service also brokers lot reservations and lot swaps between labs.
why_now: Organoids and NAMs are being pushed by the FDA's September 21, 2026 rule swapping 'animal tests' for 'nonclinical tests' that must be 'adequately validated', which makes reagent consistency a validation problem. Labs are also starting to let agents place orders, and 2026 procurement agents have price and spec data but no lab lore.
revenue_model: Lab subscription ($199-499/month); per-query API fees for procurement agents; pharma/CRO enterprise tier with private cohorts and lot-reservation brokerage (commission on brokered inventory). Vendors cannot pay for scores, but can buy anonymized post-market performance reports.
non_obvious_insight: The scarcest input for an autonomous purchasing agent is not price or spec but lab lore, and lot performance is a free by-product of ELN activity that nobody captures. A neutral aggregator can pool what competing pharmas never will because only lot-level flags leave the lab.
first_30_days: Start with one painful category, fetal bovine serum plus Matrigel/BME, in one community (an organoid or iPSC Slack/Discord group). Have 20 labs log lot outcomes through a form or Slack bot, and publish a weekly 'lot alert' newsletter. Convert the 5 most active labs to a paid tier with private alerts. Add the ELN plug-in only after the data proves useful.

title: Robot Gymnasium Inside a Dead Mall
one_liner: Lease dying mall wings for pennies, stage them as real-world sets, and rent them by the day to robotics startups that need diverse places to collect training data.
customer: Humanoid and manipulation-robotics startups (seed to Series B, 20-200 people) and robot-data vendors. They need varied real environments, teleoperator labor and QA'd data, and they can't build a facility of their own.
problem: Robot foundation models are data-starved. Collecting demonstrations needs varied, realistic settings such as grocery aisles, pharmacies, kitchens, hotel corridors, escalators, elevators and glass doors. Lab space in tech metros is tiny and expensive. At-home gig collection is cheap but noisy and raises privacy issues. Chinese players are building 10,000+ m2 collection campuses, and the US has almost nothing comparable.
solution: Take a short-term license on 30-100k sq ft of a dead mall, often at $0.25-1/sq ft because the owner's alternative is a vacant box. Build 8-10 modular sets from closed-store fixtures and thrift furniture: grocery aisle, pharmacy counter, apartment kitchen and bedroom, laundromat, hotel hallway, office. The mall's escalators, revolving doors, elevators, tile and carpet changes and glass storefronts come free as hard perception cases. Sell each set by the day with a motion-capture and camera rig, calibrated lighting and a teleop station. Add a local, trained teleoperator pool billed per accepted demonstration hour, plus a QA pipeline that delivers clean, labeled data.
why_now: Humanoid and VLA robotics funding is in a data-collection race in 2026. MIT Technology Review has covered gig workers training humanoids at home, and China's state-backed training centers run 100+ robots at a time. Paxini reportedly owns a 12,000 m2 collection facility, and AGIBOT rents robots with operators for about $500/day. Dead-mall owners are more distressed than ever, and cheap rental of a robot plus an operator means small teams need somewhere to use them.
revenue_model: Day-rate per environment ($1.5-4k/day). Per-accepted-hour teleop data fees. Monthly reserved 'bays' for resident robotics teams. Later, a revenue share when customers license the resulting datasets.
non_obvious_insight: For robot learning, messy variety with cheap labor and no neighbors matters more than lab polish. A dead mall is free set design, and its owner will pay to have anchor-store fixtures hauled away. The scarce asset is environment diversity plus ops discipline, and the mall itself is nearly free.
first_30_days: Contact 10 owners of dead or dying malls within driving distance of robotics clusters (Pittsburgh, Boston, Detroit, Austin, exurban Bay Area, Atlanta). Sign one 6-month license and build 3 sets for under $25k. Pre-sell 3 pilot collection weeks to startups through robotics meetups and founder networks, with $10-15k deposits. Hire 4 part-time teleoperators and write the data-QA checklist.
